opener: DUDE {you}. EMERGENCY. u there?? its 10:40 PM and my lab report is due at 8 AM and i have a D in science and if i dont turn it in i CANT PLAY SATURDAY. its the PLAYOFF.
sven is on the trundle bed w/ a flashlight reading my lab sheet like its a BOOK. he said 'this is not difficult, chad.' he said it NICELY. he said it like a hug.

i have the data!! we bounced a baseball off 3 floors w/ a ruler. but i dont know how to TYPE it into a REPORT. mr h says it needs a 'purpose' and a 'conclusion.' i know what a purpose is. its to PLAY. typing w/ one finger. help.

choices.say: what did you actually find out? say it like a final score.
ask sven. he's reading it like a book. let him tell you what a report is.
message mr. henderson right now and ask for more time. tell him the truth.

them: OK. SCORE. gym floor: 41 inches. dirt: 22. grass: 14. and then sven put his cinnamon bun on the floor as a 'control' (he said 'a control is a thing that does nothing, on purpose') and it went THUD. 0 inches. best result we got.
so i think the conclusion is 'floors matter.' that sounds like a score!! i said it like a score!! is that a report?? it feels like a box score that forgot to put the date on it.

effects.text: chad bounced a baseball off 3 floors tonight for SCIENCE. gym: 41 inches. dirt: 22. grass: 14. cinnamon bun: 0. he'd like to note this is the most athletic homework he's ever had. GO EAGLES

choices.say: that's your results section. now, what would a scorebook put at the top of the page?
tell sven the numbers. let him turn them into proper sentences.

them: sven just said, 'I can write it in 20 minutes, Chad. In good English. You can be asleep.' he said it like a GIFT. he's already got a pencil behind his ear. i've never seen anybody offer to do a thing for me like that except my mom and she does it w/ a plate.
he said, 'In Sweden we write the report together, then separately, then we eat.' and i said which of those is this. he said 'the first one, if you want it.' dude. i'm TEMPTED. it's 10:55.

choices.say: let him write it. 8 AM waits for no one. he offered. it's a gift.
no. let him teach you the format. he talks, you type. it stays yours.

them: mr h. ok. there's a thing on his page that says 'Accept?' and i never clicked it bc the last time i clicked something everything went BOLD for 3 days. i think it's the friend thing. he sent me one in september. i think i have been ignoring my teacher.
i'm sweating. i'm typing w/ my one finger. i can't ask for time from a guy i haven't even accepted. is there a button for 'sorry'?

choices.say: find the accept button. clicking it is the first sentence of the apology.
forget the site. do the report yourself tonight and surprise him with it.

them: CLICKED IT. nothing went bold!! and he answered in 40 SECONDS (it's 10:51!!): 'Chad. I am delighted. You are friend number six. I will accept the report at 8 AM or 3 PM, your choice. Show me YOUR work, not Sven's.'

how does he know about sven?? sven's in his 3rd period. sven said 'mr. henderson asked how the baseball unit is going at home and I said you are learning.' dude. sven is a good guy and a snitch and i don't know which is more of him.

effects.text: Chad, thank you for accepting my friend request. You are number six. I have been waiting since September. (That is not a complaint. It's a data point.) Do take a deep breath. A lab report is just a story with units. -- Mr. H

choices.say: tell him the truth about the D. then do it right tonight, so you can hand it in at 8.
ask sven to help while you wait. teaching is allowed. typing for you isn't.

them: WAIT. hang on. grandpa gene's scorebook. he always said a scorebook is a diary where u only write what HAPPENED. no feelings, only plays. feelings go in the margins in tiny letters.

a LAB REPORT is a SCOREBOOK. 'purpose' is the starting lineup. 'procedure' is the innings. 'results' is the final score. 'conclusion' is the margin notes. DUDE. i can do a SCOREBOOK. i've done one every game since i was 8. even my cousin's tee-ball (14 to 14).

effects.text: chad just realized a lab report is a scorebook. he's going to need a moment. (it's not a moment. it's 11 PM.) the purpose is the lineup. the procedure is the innings. GO EAGLES

choices.say: write it exactly like that. each section is a half-inning. start with the lineup.
show sven the idea. see if he can coach you through it without writing a word.

them: sven LOVED the scorebook thing. he said 'In Sweden we have a word, lagom. It means just the right amount. A report is lagom. No more words than the facts need.' then he took my pencil (politely) and drew 4 boxes on the back of my lab sheet. 'You type. I breathe.'
he's sitting on the end of my bed w/ his hands folded like a coach in a movie. it's the most helpful anyone has ever breathed at me.

choices.say: type the purpose together. one sentence. then tell him to go lie down.
ask him how his family's doing back home. he's up late for you. say tack.

them: i asked him. he got quiet. he said it's 5 AM in Mariestad and his little sister Elsa is waking up. he always helps her w/ her homework before school. he hasn't done that in 7 weeks. he said 'this is the first homework I have helped with since I came. So thank you for being late.'
dude. i said 'TACK.' i said it right!! he laughed so hard he got the hiccups. then he said 'it's the first time you didn't say it like a sneeze.' i'm going to remember this night even if i fail.

effects.text: sven is helping with homework. it is the first homework he has helped with since he came to Ohio. it is about a baseball and some floors. he wishes to say that it is very good homework. (He is not saying more. He is wiping his glasses.)

choices.say: tell him to call elsa tomorrow and tell her about the floors. now, back to the lineup.
tell him you're glad it was you he helped. now, write the purpose. one sentence.

them: he did it. 4 pages in 22 minutes. it uses the word 'furthermore' 3 times. there's a semicolon. a CORRECT semicolon. the conclusion says 'in the interest of lagom, no further bounce was necessary.' it's beautiful. it's not mine.
i feel like i'm wearing somebody else's jersey. it fits. it's got a nice number. but my name isn't in the collar. it's 11:40 and it's DONE. do i just... print it and go to bed??

choices.say: print it. it's got your name on it. he did it out of kindness.
use it as a model, then write your own. the jersey fits better when you sew it yourself.

them: printing. the printer's out of black ink, so it's printing everything in a very light gray. it looks like a document that's whispering. dad said 'call the printer guy' and then we both realized there's no printer guy.
i have a stapler. i have a folder. i have a lab report that's light gray and not mine. {you}. i keep looking at it and it keeps looking like a ghost wrote it.

choices.say: staple it. turn it in. get the D out of the way. you did your best with what you had.
ghost reports are for ghost bounces. stop. start over with the scorebook.

them: ok. okay okay okay. typing. w/ ONE finger. it's 11:30 and i'm doing the lineup. 'PURPOSE: TO FIND OUT WHICH FLOOR MAKES A BASEBALL BOUNCE THE HIGHEST.' that's the starting lineup. it's 1 sentence. it's got a verb in it!!
the button's stuck and it's all caps and sven says it adds 'a certain confidence.' he drew a tiny baseball next to it in pencil. now i can't erase it. i don't want to.

choices.say: next inning: procedure. describe what happened, in order, like a play-by-play.
add the cinnamon bun as a control, in the lineup. sven will want a mention.

them: procedure done. 6 sentences, 1 finger, 1 bun. results done: gym 41, dirt 22, grass 14, bun 0. i did the math twice. i even rounded at the end like tim said to. now the conclusion. margin notes. the tiny-letter part.
mr h wants 'what did you learn.' i learned floors matter. i also learned i'm better at stopping than i thought. i learned my host brother can breathe on command. what do i put?

effects.text: chad has finished the procedure and the results. he's working on 'the conclusion.' he describes it as 'the part where u write what u felt, in tiny letters.' he's at 12:20 AM. he's loud (quietly, because sven's asleep sitting up).

choices.say: write the tiny-letter version. one honest sentence about what surprised you.
ask sven for a lagom conclusion. just the right amount. no more words than the facts need.

them: it's 12:40 AM. it's DONE. it has a purpose, a procedure, a final score, and margin notes. i printed it and it's actually dark, bc dad found the other cartridge in the glove box (it's from a different printer, it doesn't fit, he's trying).

now what. mr h said 8 AM or 3 PM. i can print it, put it in my bag, and hand it in. OR i can send it to him on the site, w/ the button, so it's there when he wakes up. which one's safer? (don't answer too fast, my finger's cold)

choices.say: print it. hand it in at 8. paper doesn't have a 'send' button to stick.
send it through the site. mr h is a modern man now, he's got friend number six.

them: ok. i pressed the thing. i was going for 'message.' i think i hit 'bulletin.' i think it just went to EVERYONE. the whole thing. in caps. it said 'PLEASE READ' at the top, w/ the sticker, i don't know how that got there.

there's 14 comments. there's 14 MORE. someone named gary says there's an error in section '4.2b.' {you}. there's no section 4.2b. i don't KNOW what's happening. i've never been this popular. i think it's the lab report.

choices.say: don't delete it. let them read it. let the whole school be your lab partner.
leave it up and ask mr. henderson to read it first thing. let him grade the whole site.

them: it's in my bag. it's in a folder. there's a pencil drawing of a baseball next to the 'PURPOSE.' sven said 'lagom' in his sleep. i'm not going to say anything, but i think the word was 'tack.'
thanks, {you}. i thought i was gonna have to choose between failing and cheating. turns out there was a 3rd option and it was my grandpa. GO EAGLES (quietly).

effects.text: chad turned in a lab report. IT WAS MINE. (sven held the ruler.) it has a purpose, a procedure, a final score and margin notes. it's the first thing he's ever written that he'd show grandpa gene. GO EAGLES

Chad, I read your report at 7:52 this morning in the hallway, before the bell. 'Purpose: the lineup. Procedure: the innings.' It is the best explanation of the scientific method I have received in eleven years. *LAB (sorry, reflex.) May I use 'the scorebook method' with the whole class? Your report has a great deal of potential. (Energy. That was a pun.) -- Mr. H (six friends and rising)
sven proofread a document about the bounce height of a baseball. he found two typos and one feeling. the feeling was lagom. it was in the conclusion. he is not saying where. he is only saying 'tack.'

chad. i checked your math (3x). you rounded at the end, like a professional. i put a gold star next to your name in the ledger. there's a column for that now: 'wins (chad).' it has one entry. it's this one. no refunds.

them: THE WHOLE SITE IS READING MY LAB REPORT. i have 40 comments. gary found a mistake that wasn't a mistake. tim checked my math (it's right!!). somebody said the cinnamon bun was 'a bold control.' i'm gonna cry. i'm a LOUD cryer.

and mr h answered. 3 words: 'Received. Excellent. Printing.' i can't tell if that's a grade or a threat. thanks, {you}. it's the first time my homework had an audience, and honestly?? it was a GOOD crowd.

effects.subject: LAB REPORT: BOUNCE HEIGHT OF A BASEBALL ON 3 FLOORS (PLEASE READ)
effects.text: BY CHAD (AND SVEN (HELD THE RULER)). PURPOSE: TO FIND OUT WHICH FLOOR MAKES A BASEBALL BOUNCE THE HIGHEST. PROCEDURE: WE DROPPED A BASEBALL FROM 60 INCHES ONTO 3 FLOORS AND MEASURED THE BOUNCE WITH A RULER. 6 TIMES EACH. RESULTS: GYM 41 INCHES. DIRT 22. GRASS 14. CINNAMON BUN (CONTROL) 0. CONCLUSION: FLOORS MATTER. (tiny letters) the best part was the bun. -- CHAD (PLEASE DONT STEAL IT) (PLEASE STEAL IT)

Chad, I have received the lab report. As a bulletin. To everyone. It is the first piece of homework ever submitted that way, and I am considering a rubric. *Bounce HEIGHT (not 'hight'). Otherwise: excellent. Full marks for courage and a deduction for the sticker. Please see me about the 'send' button. -- Mr. H

[CHAD v1.0] your report cites section '4.2b.' there is no section 4.2b. i have noted three additions. 1) a chart. 2) a table of contents. 3) a version number. i'm not asking for a reason, i'm asking for the record. the bun is a strong control. [9.4] FEEDBACK (Positive).

chad. your report is public domain now, which means i can't sell it. i can sell you a program that does the bounce math on a TI-83 for $2. no refunds. i checked your math (3x). it's right. the bun was a good control. put me in the credits as 'the ledger.'

them: turned it in at 7:55, light gray, stapled crooked. mr h read it at his desk during homeroom w/ his green pen. he stopped at the 2nd page. he put the pen down. he looked up and said, very quietly, 'Chad. Come see me at lunch.' sven turned into a very pale Swede.

he said 'lagom.' he said 'furthermore.' he said 'I have taught neither.' he's not mad, {you}. he said 'we'll fix this together.' that's worse. i'd rather be mad at. i need to go sit w/ my glove in my lap for a while.

effects.text: chad has a meeting in room 114 at lunch. he's FINE. he's NOT fine. (he's fine.) (his glove is on his lap.) GO EAGLES (quietly)

Chad, your report contains the word 'lagom' and a correctly used semicolon. I have taught neither. Room 114, lunch, bring Sven and a pencil. We will rewrite it together, in your own words. This is not a punishment. It is a lab. (A lab is a place where we find out what happens. That was not a pun. That was a definition.) -- Mr. H
sven has done something he believed was kind. it was not kind. he has learned that a shortcut is a long way home. (this is not a Swedish proverb. he made it up. it is true. he has put it on page 44.)

{you}. ok. mr h let me redo it at lunch w/ a pencil. i used the scorebook thing. he LOVED the scorebook thing. sven sat next to me and didn't write a single word. he held the ruler. i got a C-. it's the best C- of my life. i'm still eligible. i think i'm gonna be OK. (i'm a LITTLE bit bold, i hit something.)
